_BASELINE_INTERPRETATION_:
- **MLP: 52.8% val / 53.0% test.** Much better than chance (10%), because colour and rough layout already say a lot (§3). But it overfits from the start: train accuracy reaches 86% while val loss is minimal at epoch 4 and then *grows* from 1.41 to 2.4. 3.7 M parameters with no notion of neighbouring pixels memorise the training set.
- **Simple CNN: 70.9% / 70.5%** with **22× fewer parameters** (168 k). Weight sharing and locality are the right prior for images: +18 percentage points over the MLP. It also overfits (val loss minimal at epoch 9, train–val gap 19 pp at the end).
- **Deep CNN (BN + Dropout): 85.3% / 85.2%**, the best baseline model. Its train and val curves stay close (gap 4 pp), val loss keeps decreasing — it is still improving at epoch 20, so it is regularised rather than overfitting.
- **SE-CNN: 72.4% / 72.7%.** It is the simple 2-conv network plus channel attention; +1.5 pp over the simple CNN with a similar depth, but far below the deep CNN: attention re-weights features, it cannot replace depth (only two conv layers ⇒ small receptive field). It overfits too: no BN, one Dropout.

Ranking by test accuracy matches the validation ranking, so the validation set is a reliable guide.
_ABLATION_INTERPRETATION_:
Validation-accuracy deltas (the std error of an accuracy on 5 000 images is ≈0.5 pp, so differences below ~1 pp are noise):

| Step | val acc | Δ | What the curves show |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain deep CNN | 77.7% | — | train 98%, val loss explodes after epoch 6 (0.68 → 1.51): classic overfitting |
| + BatchNorm only | 82.8% | +5.1 | faster and higher, but still memorises (train 99%, val loss grows) |
| + Dropout only | 80.7% | +3.0 | overfitting gone (gap 1 pp), but learns slowly |
| BN + Dropout (baseline) | 85.3% | +7.6 vs plain | BN speeds up, Dropout prevents memorising — they complement each other |
| + augmentation | 86.6% | +1.3 | train acc now *below* val (harder augmented data + dropout); still improving at epoch 20 |
| + SE attention | 86.4% | −0.2 | no measurable gain in an already deep, regularised net |
| Adam → SGD + OneCycle | 87.9% | +1.3 | lower val loss (0.35 vs 0.39) |
| 2× wider (2.2 M params) | 90.5% | +2.6 | more filters per layer = more features; the biggest single gain after BN+Dropout |

**Biggest contributors:** BatchNorm + Dropout together (+7.6 pp) and model capacity once overfitting is controlled (+2.6 pp). Augmentation gives a modest +1.3 pp in 20 epochs, but it changes the regime: the augmented models are not overfitting at all, so they would keep improving with more epochs, while non-augmented ones had already peaked.
_FINAL_INTERPRETATION_: **ResNet-9: 93.0% validation, 92.6% test** — +7.4 pp over the best baseline model and +2.0 pp over the wide CNN, with fewer parameters than the wide CNN (1.66 M vs 2.2 M). Residual connections let the network be deeper (8 conv layers in the main path) without the optimisation problems of a plain deep stack. The OneCycle schedule is visible in the curves: val accuracy stalls around 79–83% while the learning rate is high (epochs 7–16), then climbs from 85% to 93% in the last third as the lr decays. Train accuracy (98%, measured on augmented images) is above val, so with more epochs or stronger augmentation (e.g. Cutout) the model could still improve. The test result (92.6%) is close to the reported human level (~94%).
_COMPARISON_INTERPRETATION_: Test accuracy follows validation accuracy everywhere (max difference 0.6 pp), so model selection on validation did not overfit the validation set. Progression: **MLP 53% → simple CNN 70.5% → baseline deep CNN 85.2% → + augmentation and OneCycle 87.8% → wider 90.6% → ResNet-9 92.6%.** Parameter count is not what decides: the MLP has the most parameters and is the worst; ResNet-9 has fewer parameters than the wide CNN and is better. The architecture's inductive bias (locality, weight sharing, residual paths) and regularisation decide.
_ERRORS_INTERPRETATION_: Per-class recall ranges from **83.9% (cat)** to **97.5% (automobile)**. The hardest classes are the animals with similar texture and pose: cat (83.9%), dog (86.7%), bird (89.4%). The top confusions are **dog→cat (81) and cat→dog (66)** — together 147 of 743 errors (20%). Next: bird↔frog/cat (small brownish animals on grass), airplane→ship (blue background), truck→automobile (pickups and SUVs are on the border between the two classes). The vehicles and horse/ship are above 94%. These are exactly the pairs that looked similar in the EDA (mean images, colour table).
_REVIEW_NOTE_: Looking at the grid above: several mistakes are understandable even for a human (a seagull over water predicted as *ship*, a red vintage car predicted as *truck*, pickups predicted as *automobile*, dark close-ups of cats and dogs). The verdict column is left for manual review.
_TSNE_INTERPRETATION_: Penultimate-layer features form 10 clear clusters: the network has turned 3 072 raw pixels into a space where classes are almost linearly separable — that is what the final Dense layer needs. The only clusters that touch are **cat–dog** (and cat touching bird/frog), **airplane–ship** and **truck–automobile**, the same pairs as in the confusion matrix. Vehicles lie on one side, animals on the other.
_CONCLUSION_:
1. **Data.** CIFAR-10 is clean and perfectly balanced (5 000/1 000 images per class, all 32×32×3, no duplicates), so accuracy is a fair metric. The difficulty is visual: low resolution, varied poses, similar classes (cat/dog, automobile/truck, airplane/ship).
2. **Why CNNs.** On the same data the baseline MLP reaches 53%, a 2-layer CNN with 22× fewer parameters 70.5%: locality and weight sharing are the right assumptions for images.
3. **What helped** (one change at a time, on validation): BatchNorm + Dropout +7.6 pp (they fix overfitting differently and complement each other), augmentation +1.3 pp (and removes overfitting entirely), SGD + OneCycle +1.3 pp, 2× width +2.6 pp. SE attention gave +1.5 pp in the small network but nothing measurable in the deep one.
4. **Best model:** ResNet-9 with SE blocks, augmentation, OneCycle and label smoothing — **92.6% test accuracy** (baseline deep CNN: 85.2%), loss 0.31. Remaining errors are mostly cat↔dog.
5. **Validation protocol:** model choice on a 5 000-image validation split; test accuracy differs from validation by ≤0.6 pp for every model.
6. **Limitations:** one seed per experiment (differences < 1 pp are within noise); 20 epochs for the ablation (the augmented models were still improving); the Mac ran in Low Power Mode, so the times are not representative.
7. **Next steps:** more epochs, Cutout/MixUp, test-time augmentation (flip), full-width ResNet-9 on a cloud GPU (≈94%). The CIFAR-100 run is in `cifar100_resnet9.ipynb`.
